review_evidence: Inspected the hydrated ACL2 unit across all 166 currently primary files. Direct event scanning found substantive definitions/theorems/interfaces in sources such as books/projects/hexnet/example-network.lsp, books/projects/hexnet/helper-functions.lisp, books/projects/hexnet/hexnet-model.lisp; nonempty .sys proof-use metadata remains searchable.

Complete-file screening covered the 28 primary non-.sys files without common declaration-event forms and distinguished 17 exact certification/customization/portcullis wrappers from retained utilities, executable specifications, documentation, examples/tests, and specialized support files. Representative retained declaration-light files include books/projects/pfcs/oset-lib-ext.lisp, books/projects/pfcs/r1cs-lib-ext.lisp, books/projects/pltpa/chk-jacm-proveall.acl2.

The hard-exclusion selector is intentionally limited to canonical setup/certification wrapper basenames whose full contents contain no definition/theorem/package/event forms. Import/top files, formal examples/tests, project documentation, solver/checker/translator code, and nonstandard support files remain retained unless separately proven lossless.

rules.content_invariant: Every selected file was inspected completely and contains only package/book loading, certification/customization setup, or portcullis context for separately retained formal sources; no selected file owns a definition, theorem, package declaration, proof, reusable formal interface, or standalone formal example.
evidence: Complete-file inspection covered all 17 selected wrapper files in this review unit.

Direct-event sources, formal examples/tests, project developments, specialized solver/checker/translator files, navigation/documentation not proven redundant, and nonempty proof metadata remain outside the selector.
rules.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certification, customization, and portcullis wrappers from primary formalization search.

summary: Reviewed this ACL2 project unit. Formal definitions/theorems, executable/project specifications, examples/tests, proof developments, documentation, specialized interfaces, and proof metadata remain searchable; only exact declaration-free setup/certification wrappers are excluded.
